applications.name: GNU grep
applications.summary: Command-line matching of fixed strings and regular expressions in text streams and files, with explicit recursive-search and output controls.
applications.license: GNU General Public License v3.0 or later
strengths: Explicit line-oriented output fits shell pipelines and existing command-line scripts.
limitations: Recursive search does not automatically apply Git ignore rules.
Locale, binary handling, regex dialect and output options affect results and must be aligned before comparing tools.
The recorded performance experiment uses GNU grep 3.11; it does not test every current release or operating system.
use_cases: Filter text streams and search file contents with predictable command-line options.
applications.platform_notes: Linux packaging was verified through Ubuntu and the installed Linux executable. Upstream distributes portable source; other operating-system builds are not established by this record.
applications.pricing_notes: The official source archive is publicly downloadable without payment. Distribution packages and optional commercial support have separate terms.

recommendation.pick_for: Use line-oriented matching in shell pipelines and scripts with explicit search flags.
recommendation.compare_when: Consider ripgrep for repository ignore-file awareness; inspect the scoped measurement rather than assuming a universal speed winner.

maintenance.note: The inspected stable release announcement is grep 3.12 from April 2025; this source does not establish current release cadence.
